---
slug: one_whole_week
title: One Whole Week
blurb: Stuck on a junk asteroid for a week, Sanya teleports to her private Floran temple for peace, only to find it overrun by marauders and one very unbothered stranger named Mary.
authors: Brody
season: FF3
format: prose
---

One whole week. Sanya would be stuck on this trash heap of an asteroid for an entire week. Sanya was fine dealing with this horrorshow of a crew for smaller increments, and when she had her own private time, but this would be too much. Sanya got up from her bed and plopped down at her desk. It was late, and she was certain the rest of the crew was asleep. “[I have all this time, so I might as well do a bit of research.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Reaching down to the bottom shelf, she grabbed a small device taped to the top of the shelf. With a small click, Sanya activated the teleporter.

Her destination was an ancient Floran Temple, a housing place of her Floran research. She had discovered it early in her research and promptly sought it out. As Sanya phased into her home away from home, she took a quick glance to make sure nothing had been touched. Her sleeping bag, her stack of books, her food-. The food was gone. She wasn’t alone. “[Show yourselves, now.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” She drew her blade, glancing around the temple’s main chamber. She could tell it was more than one. The books were rearranged, there were plenty of tracks in the sand by the entrance, and all of her food was gone. *Focus. Listen. There!* Sanya threw her knife at a rustle, and hit something dead on. “[Damn it! Jump her!]{Marauder}” As the body fell, around 9 to 10 more marauders came from the shadows, surrounding Sanya. [*You’re outnumbered, even for a trained assassin. You know what you have to do, but you won’t do it.*]{Dread} No choice. She had to release her fear gas, despite the repercussions. This was her only choice.

[*It’s time to let me in, Sanya. You know you had to let me in eventually. Now, don’t worry about a thing. This will be easy...*]{Dread} The flower opened its mouth, and a viscous black liquid began to pour out. Sanya’s body went limp, and as the liquid hit the ground and formed gas, she raised herself in an upright position. “[Now, you have made the fatal mistake of attempting to fight me. I’d warn you of my Assassin training, but warnings are useless now. Make peace with the life you lead now, for it’s over.]{Dread}” Sanya cracked a smile, more viscous liquid falling from her agape mouth. But, as the two readied their blades, a sharp cry rang from the crowd. A body had fallen, but not by Sanya. This mysterious woman only yelled “[I like your style! Let’s get to it.]{Mary}” Unconcerned by the turning of this new ally, Sanya cut through the enemies quickly, as if they were nothing. Pleas for mercy rang through the emptying halls of the temple, as blood once again flowed down the cracks in the stonework.

As the last body fell, Sanya looked at her new partner, and realized something. “[Why weren't you affected by our fear gas?]{Dread}” “[I’m not sure what you mean by *our,* but to be honest, being scared makes me a bit… excited.]{Mary}” [*Our? No, wait, not again. I am me, Sanya. There is no we, there is no our-*]{Sanya Dreadflower} Sanya fell to the ground, desperately trying to separate her from herself. “[Hey, Red, are you ok? I didn’t know you were into that sort of thing. I guess I better watch what I say around you, huh? Red?]{Mary}” The woman outstretched her hand to help the Floran up. “[Our name-]{Dread}” “[My name is Sanya, not Red.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”” Sanya pulled herself up, ignoring her new friend’s attempt to help. “[Why did you turn on your own crew? And how do I know I can actually trust you?]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya dusted herself off and began to tidy up the now bloodied room. “[The name’s Mary, seeing how you didn’t ask. As for the backstabbing, well… I didn’t really like those guys. What better reason do you need?]{Mary}” Mary plopped down on the set of stairs and watched as Sanya started to stuff the bodies into her food barrel. “[So, Red, what do you do?]{Mary}”

“[I’m an assassin. I work for a crew of mercenaries.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya sat on her sleeping bag and cracked open a nearby book. “[I’m a Floran, and I was interested in ancient Floran culture, so I set up base here in this temple. I came because my crew is currently stuck on a junk heap for a whole week. I thought that I would have some privacy here.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya glared at Mary, taking the first good look at her. She was an angel, a winged humanoid race. Dressed in a silver and gold outfit, her pink hair stood out from the drab tans and dark reds of the temple. “[Oh, don’t worry about me. I’ll make sure I won’t bother you *too* much. But, this will definitely be a fun week! I'm guessing you won’t be staying?]{Mary}” “[That’s right, I won’t stay the whole week.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” “[Can I use your sleeping bag while you’re gone?]{Mary}”

***

“[Fine.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”
